name: Independent on Sunday cryptic crossword No 1,761

entries.clue: Celeb stories - not one surprises (8)

indicators.note: 'not' tells you to remove, and 'one' is A

blocks.note: a celeb is a star
stories = tales

annotation.surface: A gossip magazine promising celebrity stories that turn out to contain no surprises at all.
annotation.walkthrough: The dash makes 'not one surprises' look like a verdict on the stories; in fact 'surprises' is a verb and the definition, and 'one' is the A to drop.
annotation.definitionFit: To startle someone is to surprise them.

entries.clue: Travelled over there to cover middle of the US game (6-3)

indicators.note: the new letters are laid over the middle of THE, hiding its H

blocks.note: used as written
travelled = went
yon = over there, old-fashioned

annotation.surface: Someone who crossed the country to report on the middle of America.
annotation.walkthrough: 'The US' reads as America, but 'the' is working letters and 'US' belongs to the definition: twenty-one is the American name for the card game the British call pontoon or vingt-et-un.
annotation.definitionFit: Twenty-one, also called blackjack, is the usual American name for the card game.

entries.clue: Hit, cut, flog and cane (5)

indicators.note: cutting a word takes off its last letter

blocks.note: hit = RAM, cut short to RA
to tan someone's hide is to flog them

annotation.surface: A list of old schoolroom punishments: hitting, cutting, flogging and caning.
annotation.walkthrough: Every word looks like one more item in a list of beatings, so 'cane' hides as a verb; it is a noun here, the definition. Ratan is a less common spelling of rattan.
annotation.definitionFit: Ratan (rattan) is a climbing palm whose stems are used as canes.

entries.clue: Religious pronouncement made by St Paul, ye righteous, in the beginning (3,2,4)

indicators.note: the letters are made into something new
take only the start of 'righteous'

blocks.note: anagram fodder
first letter of righteous

annotation.surface: A solemn saying attributed to St Paul addressing the righteous, perhaps from Genesis.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface sounds like scripture, and 'made by St Paul' seems to name an author; 'made' is the instruction to rearrange his name with YE and R.
annotation.definitionFit: "Let us pray" is the priest's call to prayer in a church service.

entries.clue: Getting hard? It's what I'm doing (7)

blocks.note: what concrete or jelly does as it firms up
'I' in a crossword is its compiler, and this is what a compiler does to a puzzle

annotation.surface: A cheeky question and answer that reads like innuendo.
annotation.walkthrough: In crosswords 'I' or 'me' is often the setter, so what I am doing is setting the puzzle.
annotation.definitionFit: Glue and cement set, getting hard; a setter sets crosswords.

entries.clue: Browser chat (6)

blocks.note: a browser here is an animal that nibbles grass and shoots
British slang for chattering on, from rhyming slang for talk

annotation.surface: Two computer words: a web browser and online chat.
annotation.walkthrough: Both words now suggest the internet, but a browser here is an animal that feeds on plants, and rabbit is British slang for idle talk.
annotation.definitionFit: Rabbits browse on vegetation, and 'rabbiting on' is British for talking at length.

entries.clue: Police escort learner initially follows on drive back (5)

indicators.note: take the first letter of each of the three words before it
those letters come after RE

blocks.note: re = on, concerning
first letters of Police, escort, learner

annotation.surface: A learner driver escorted by police taking a test drive back home.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Learner' looks like L on its own, but 'initially' covers all three words before it; 'drive back' reads as a journey but means repulse.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: repelling invaders means forcing them to retreat.

entries.clue: Boycott toys making comeback in dangerous locality (5,4)

indicators.note: coming back means turning round

blocks.note: to black goods is to boycott them, a trade-union term
spinning tops are toys

annotation.surface: A campaign to boycott toys making a return somewhere dangerous.
annotation.walkthrough: Boycott suggests Geoffrey Boycott the cricketer, but it is the verb. A black spot is British for a stretch of road where accidents cluster.
annotation.definitionFit: An accident black spot is a place known to be dangerous.

entries.clue: Does nothing much, and did less when contracted (5)

indicators.note: contracting a phrase shortens it, here by one letter at each end

blocks.note: used as written

annotation.surface: A slacker who does little, and did even less once signed to a contract.
annotation.walkthrough: The wordplay half reads as a second definition of laziness, which it is too: DID LESS trimmed at both ends.
annotation.definitionFit: Someone who idles does very little.

entries.clue: Group hanky-panky gets offensive (6)

blocks.note: hanky-panky is sexual goings-on
the Tet Offensive of the Vietnam War, 1968

annotation.surface: A tabloid line: group hanky-panky turning offensive.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Offensive' reads as an adjective; it is the noun, the Tet Offensive, supplying TET.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by category: a set of six performers is one particular kind of group.

entries.clue: Supply pistols - a 21 might raise them (8)

indicators.note: read as supple-ly, flexibly, the letters bent into a new order

blocks.note: anagram fodder

annotation.surface: An arms dealer's note: supply the pistols, since a jack might need to raise them.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Supply' is not the verb but an adverb, 'in a supple way'. The 21 is 21 across, JACK, a sailor, who would hoist the sails.
annotation.definitionFit: Topsails are sails set above the mainsail, raised by sailors (jacks).

entries.clue: Halt, having shot pursuing bear (10)

indicators.note: one piece chases the other, so it comes after

blocks.note: to bear something is to stand it
a still is a single photographic shot

annotation.surface: A hunter's command to stop once a shot has been fired at a pursuing bear.
annotation.walkthrough: The bear is not an animal but the verb 'tolerate', and the shot is from a camera, not a gun.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: traffic that has come to a complete stop, not moving at all.

entries.clue: Snog Kay, young lady Mike dumped (4)

indicators.note: Mike is thrown out of the word

blocks.note: the letter K is spelt kay
a miss is a young woman
MISS loses M (Mike in the phonetic alphabet), leaving ISS

annotation.surface: Kay snogs a young lady who dumped Mike.
annotation.walkthrough: Kay and Mike look like people in a love triangle, but both are letter names: K spelt out, and M in the radio alphabet.
annotation.definitionFit: Snog is British slang for a long kiss.

entries.clue: Throw a wobbly, causing open conflict (3,3)

indicators.note: unsteady letters fall into a new order

blocks.note: anagram fodder

annotation.surface: A tantrum that escalates into open conflict.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Throw a wobbly' is British for losing your temper, so the phrase reads as one idiom; split it, and 'wobbly' shakes up THROW A.
annotation.definitionFit: A hot war is open fighting, as opposed to a cold war.

entries.clue: Kind of wine regularly sampled at source, it's noted (4,5)

indicators.note: at regular intervals, so every second letter is sampled
the sampled letters are placed after the source

blocks.note: a well is a source of water
every other letter of KiNd Of WiNe

annotation.surface: A wine taster explaining that a particular type was sampled at the vineyard.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Kind of wine' looks like it wants a grape or style; it is just fodder for regular letters.
annotation.definitionFit: Noted in the sense of famous or distinguished, as in 'a noted author'.

entries.clue: Government file concerned with reaching good understanding (8)

indicators.note: the pieces run on until they reach the last one

blocks.note: G is the abbreviation for government
a rasp is a coarse file
in = involved with, as in 'in shipping'
G = good

annotation.surface: A government dossier about reaching an understanding between parties.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Government file' reads as a dossier, but the file is a tool, a rasp.
annotation.definitionFit: The figurative sense of seizing: taking an idea firmly in hand mentally.

entries.clue: Type of protective software zapped Sun trivia (9)

indicators.note: blasted, the letters scattered

blocks.note: anagram fodder

annotation.surface: Security software that blocks trivia from The Sun, a British tabloid.
annotation.walkthrough: The italics make Sun the newspaper, which suits the surface; the letters are all that matter.
annotation.definitionFit: Antivirus software protects a computer from malicious programs.

entries.clue: Stone urn I pounded into tiny bits (9)

indicators.note: letters smashed into a new form

blocks.note: anagram fodder

annotation.surface: Someone smashing a stone urn to fragments.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is all about rubble, and the definition sits there as the size of the fragments; the answer is physics, particles with almost no mass.
annotation.definitionFit: A playful description: these subatomic particles, nearly massless, are among the smallest pieces of matter physics knows.

entries.clue: Fabric set down, picked up and put on again (8)

indicators.note: heard, so the word is taken by sound

blocks.note: rep is a ribbed fabric used in upholstery
set down = laid, spelt the way it sounds

annotation.surface: Fabric laid down, lifted and put back on again, like a dust sheet.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Picked up' looks like the opposite of 'set down', completing a little story of handling fabric; it is the sound signal.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for a record, film or match shown or played a second time.

entries.clue: Put on spectacles after idiot dropped small IT accessories (7)

indicators.note: the glasses come after DON
something dropped falls out, so ASS leaves GLASSES

blocks.note: to don clothes is to put them on
spectacles = glasses
GLASSES drops ASS (idiot), leaving GLES

annotation.surface: An idiot drops their glasses and fumbles with the computer gadgets.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Put on spectacles' reads as a single action and 'idiot' as an insult to the wearer; in fact the idiot is a three-letter word lifted out of the eyewear.
annotation.definitionFit: Dongles are small devices that plug into a computer port.

entries.clue: Counts sheep jumping over the stile, at first (4,2)

indicators.note: the sheep straddles the letters, going round them
each of the three words gives what it has at first, its opening letter

blocks.note: a tup is a ram
first letters of over, the, stile

annotation.surface: Counting sheep as they jump a stile, the classic way to fall asleep.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is the insomniac's routine, which also defines the answer; 'over' is not part of the jump but one of the three words for first letters.
annotation.definitionFit: To tot up is to add up, count.

entries.clue: Standard rating (4)

blocks.note: a standard is a flag, like the small one flown at a ship's bow
a rating is an ordinary sailor, not an officer

annotation.walkthrough: Both words look like measures of quality; a standard is a flag and a rating is a naval rank below officer.
annotation.definitionFit: A jack is a ship's flag and also a sailor.

entries.clue: Float high in the sky (5)

indicators.note: high as in intoxicated, the letters out of their minds

blocks.note: anagram fodder

annotation.surface: A balloon floating high in the sky.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue reads as one image; 'high' belongs with it naturally but is the anagram signal.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both describe something high overhead, up in the air.

entries.clue: During late autumn, one on the Right's bringing new ideas (10)

blocks.note: during = in
November, abbreviated
one = a
a Tory is a British Conservative, on the political right

annotation.surface: A political note that in late autumn a right-winger is floating fresh ideas.
annotation.walkthrough: The 's is 'is', joining wordplay to definition. NOV is the calendar abbreviation.
annotation.definitionFit: Innovatory means introducing new ideas or methods.

entries.clue: Having insignificant substance in bread - that's sandwiches (5)

indicators.note: IE goes either side of NAN, like bread round a filling

blocks.note: i.e. = that is
nan (naan) is Indian flatbread

annotation.surface: A sandwich with barely anything of substance between the slices.
annotation.walkthrough: The joke is that the bread is the filling here and 'that's' is the slices.
annotation.definitionFit: Inane means empty, lacking sense or substance.

entries.clue: Time (start of Yuletide) to drink rum with hot beverage (5)

indicators.note: T and Y take ODD inside, as if swallowing it

blocks.note: T = time, plus Y, the first letter of Yuletide
rum = odd, strange

annotation.surface: At the start of Christmas it's time for rum with a hot drink.
annotation.walkthrough: Rum is a spirit in a toddy, which makes it the perfect decoy: here it is the adjective meaning strange.
annotation.definitionFit: A toddy is a hot drink of spirits, water, sugar and spices.

entries.clue: Woman in crashed limo finds another mode of transport (8)

indicators.note: a woman in a car sits inside it, so NORA sits inside the crashed letters
the letters of LIMO are wrecked into a new order

blocks.note: LIMO wrecked into a new order
a woman's name

annotation.surface: A woman whose limousine crashed has to find another way to get about.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Another' works as the definition's hint that a limo is transport too.
annotation.definitionFit: A monorail is a railway running on a single rail.

entries.clue: Up in Yorkshire area, once? (6)

blocks.note: a jockey who is up is on horseback and moving
Yorkshire was split into three divisions, North, East and West, until 1974

annotation.walkthrough: Yorkshire is a county in northern England; its old North, East and West Ridings were administrative divisions, which is why 'once' is there.
annotation.definitionFit: Up on a horse means riding it, and a Riding was a former division of Yorkshire.

entries.clue: Extra ton (cement blocks) - straightaway! (2,4)

indicators.note: the words enclose the answer, stopping it being seen

blocks.note: hidden in extrA TON CEment

annotation.surface: A builder demanding an extra ton of cement blocks immediately.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cement blocks' reads as building blocks; 'blocks' is the verb, holding the answer inside the words.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both mean immediately, without any delay.

entries.clue: Bold and spirited Natasha finally leaving for Brunel - is husband like a big girl's blouse? (8)

indicators.note: one letter goes and another takes its place

blocks.note: sassy = cheeky, spirited
the A (last letter of Natasha) is replaced by I, the setter Brunel
used as written
H = husband

annotation.surface: Bold Natasha walks out on her husband and asks whether he is a wimp.
annotation.walkthrough: Brunel is this puzzle's setter, so he is I. A big girl's blouse is British slang for a weak or cowardly man.
annotation.definitionFit: A regional idiom: 'big girl's blouse' is British slang for a weak or timid man, and the answer describes that kind of behaviour.
